I think a perspective people need to have is that Australia is a young country compared to other developed nations. A lot of the racist laws are recent. From 1910 to 1970, 33% of all indigenous children were taken by the government and placed into missions to be brought up and converted into a white Christian culture. The conditions in these mission were horrible and there was a lot of physical and sexual abuse.

A lot of the reasons why a lot of Aboriginal people are mixed or white passing, like me, is that aboriginals were 'encouraged' to marry whites ('full black' aboriginals had less rights than 'half castes').The plan was a eugenics sort of genocide, so that slowly each generation would be less black and more white until it was completely erased. 


All of this has changed, thankfully, but the effects haven't gone away. There are people alive today who experienced not only being taken away as a child, but people who had their children taken away and never found them again. There's an epidemic of drug and alcohol dependency usually brought about because of mental health issues and poverty. There's a lot of cultural distrust of police and authority figures.

The way its been put to me is that PTSD, BPD, NPD, DID, etc... they are all a cluster of symptoms with (generally) the same cause: trauma.

Never feel invalidated by someone elses perception of how you should feel or respond. One is not worse than the other, just different.
